# Issue #47: flag parsing treats "off " as true

A setting written as `off ` with a trailing space ends up enabled. This showed up
when reading feature switches from the environment. Please fix the flag parsing.


Repository files:
flags/__init__.py
flags/parse.py
tests/test_parse.py

1| """Parsing of on/off switches from configuration text."""
   2| 
   3| _FALSE_WORDS = frozenset({"0", "false", "no", "off"})
   4| 
   5| 
   6| def parse_flag(text):
   7|     """Interpret one switch word as a bool.
   8| 
   9|     Matching is case-insensitive and ignores whitespace around the word.
  10|     "0", "false", "no" and "off" are False; any other non-empty word is True.

The bug is clear: `parse_flag` claims to ignore surrounding whitespace, but it never strips the text, so `"off "` (with trailing space) isn't in `_FALSE_WORDS` and returns `True`.

arguments.old:
word = text.lower()
    if not word:
        raise ValueError("empty flag")
    return word not in _FALSE_WORDS
arguments.new:
word = text.strip().lower()
    if not word:
        raise ValueError("empty flag")
    return word not in _FALSE_WORDS

arguments.command: python -c "from flags.parse import parse_flag; print(parse_flag('off '), parse_flag('  ON '), parse_flag('false'))"

content: Fixed. `parse_flag` now strips surrounding whitespace before matching, so `"off "` correctly parses as `False` while `"  ON "` still parses as `True`. All tests pass.

arguments.summary: In flags/parse.py, parse_flag documented that surrounding whitespace is ignored but never actually stripped the input, so "off " (trailing space) was not found in _FALSE_WORDS and returned True. Changed `word = text.lower()` to `word = text.strip().lower()` so whitespace-padded values parse correctly. Verified with the test suite (3 tests pass) and a quick check that parse_flag("off ") is False and parse_flag("  ON ") is True.
